A1.justification: Both complete, readable 11-page PDFs describe the same Anny research. Their text, equations, figures and tables support reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; both end with references.

before.justification: v1 reports original adult and child scan-fitting results, mesh-mapping errors, and HMR experiments in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds GPU runtime and memory measurements in Section 7 and Figure 8.

M1.justification: The phenotype interpolation, kinematics, skinning, collision checking, WHO calibration and mesh-mapping procedures are retained. v2 newly documents coarse-mesh and phenotype-count configurations, without establishing a change to the underlying method. Revised base-mesh counts explicitly use a different convention for including eyes and tongue.

E1.justification: The training datasets, scan-fitting data, HMR benchmarks and adult/child coverage are retained. The added runtime experiment varies batch sizes and model configurations, without introducing a new dataset, population or reconstruction task.

E2.justification: New Figure 8 evaluates SMPL and two SMPL-X configurations against Anny for computational cost. The existing accuracy-comparison membership is unchanged. Table 2's SMIL-X becomes SMPL-X+A with matching settings and identical scores, supporting a naming correction rather than a replacement baseline.

E3.justification: Section 7 introduces a forward-pass timing and peak-memory protocol on an NVIDIA A100, varying batch size through 8192 and testing different phenotype counts and mesh resolutions. Existing accuracy metrics, AGORA splits and stated HMR settings are retained. The six-phenotype HMR configuration is newly disclosed, not established as a changed setting.

E4.justification: Figure 8 adds an efficiency sensitivity analysis examining batch-size scaling and the effects of reducing phenotype count and mesh resolution. Existing body-model/training-data ablations and qualitative reconstruction examples remain; no new accuracy robustness or failure-case analysis is introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new runtime curves add no such reporting. Figure 5 retains the WHO population intervals, which are distinct from uncertainty estimates for experimental performance.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–3 and the scan-fitting errors are unchanged. Section 7 newly reports computational results, including 49 ms for full Anny versus 4 ms for SMPL-X for one person, 14 ms for six-phenotype Anny, and approximately 3 GB versus 11 GB at batch size 8192.

T1.justification: The interpolation description, sparse mesh-regression equation and statistical calibration formulation are retained. Neither version contains formal theorems or proofs, and the runtime addition introduces no new mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain an interpretable, unified, scan-free body model, the 800k-image Anny-One dataset, and competitive scan fitting and HMR. The abstract's correction from 'humans' to 'images' matches the existing dataset description; terminology refinements do not materially alter the claims.

C2.justification: Section 7 newly acknowledges small-batch latency overhead, attributes better large-batch scaling and memory use to the Warp implementation, and explains computational savings from reduced configurations. Existing qualifications about phenotype stereotypes, population biases and clothing-related fitting limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 discloses the six named HMR phenotype parameters, the full 267-parameter configuration, and a coarse configuration with 1,229 vertices and 36 bones. It specifies Blender Cycles, runtime hardware and the comparator implementation, and clarifies mesh-count conventions. Code-access information and Apache 2.0 licensing remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds a Blender Foundation reference and corrects the description of the child-capable interpolation model to SMPL-X+A. The broader related-work coverage and positioning against scan-based body models remain stable; reference renumbering and metadata corrections do not constitute further substantive changes.

P1.justification: There are localized prose edits, terminology corrections and a tighter abstract. A Runtime Performance section is inserted before the conclusion. The original narrative and section sequence are otherwise retained, without extensive rewriting or reorganization.

P2.justification: v2 adds the two-panel runtime/memory Figure 8 and expands Figure 4 with a coarse-mesh illustration. It refreshes the opening render, revises calibration-plot and error-scale presentation, and compacts/repositions tables. The previous qualitative Figure 8 becomes Figure 9 with the same examples.

improvement.justification: The added efficiency measurements make practical costs clearer, including unfavorable small-batch latency alongside large-batch memory benefits. Disclosure of the six-parameter HMR configuration also improves reproducibility. These are useful, limited gains: the principal accuracy evidence is unchanged, and timing/repetition details remain sparse.
